attributes.law_screen: claim.law.parameter-save-area-width-sets-the-local-block-floor.20260901.v1 SCREENED and NOT APPLICABLE BY ITS OWN DISCRIMINATOR. That law post-dates both prior parks and names a lever neither considered (the parameter save area rather than the local inventory), which is exactly the 'new law reaches a parked function' condition — so it was screened rather than assumed dead. Its stated test is: run slotdiff, and if the frame size AGREES while slots are displaced the floor is wrong and the parameter list is the lever; if the frame size DIFFERS it is the ordinary pad/declaration-count problem. Measured: frame DIFFERS (target 48, ours 56), so the precondition fails and the parameter-list audit is not indicated. Corroborating: the declared list (void*, void*, int, int) = 16 bytes is already correct — all four parameters are used, and every one of the eight call sites in this TU passes four arguments. claim.law.inlined-callee-frames-reserve-dead-frame-bottom.20260831.v1 and claim.law.inline-frame-candidates-need-a-target-minus-ours-delta-census.20260831.v1 SCREENED and NOT APPLICABLE, and this is the more interesting negative: the delta variant is the correct instrument here and it gives target-minus-ours = 20 - 28 = -8, a NEGATIVE delta, whose documented meaning is 'we inline where the original did not'. That would have been a live hypothesis, and neither prior park screened it. It is refuted by direct inspection: src/game/ps2/fakelib.c contains NO static inline function and NO pragma of any kind (its only macro, SCEHANDLE, is not reached from this function), so there is no expansion site anywhere in the TU and the inline-frame mechanism cannot be producing the reservation. claim.law.regnorm-counts-reloc-annotation-rows-as-structural.20260831.v1 APPLIED to discount four of the nine structural rows. claim.law.classify-labels-overcount-work-by-an-order-of-magnitude.20260831.v1 APPLIED to identify those four as the jumptable name-normalization artifact. claim.law.dead-nominal-local-area-tracks-declaration-count.20260831.v1 and claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order.20260831.v1 carried forward from the superseded parks unchanged. claim.law.a-lone-dead-stack-word-is-usually-the-alignment-pad-of-the-first-8-byte-temp.20260901.v1 SCREENED, not applicable: slotdiff shows equal slot COUNTS with a uniform shift, not one exclusive slot per side.
attributes.residual: UNCHANGED at real 10, insns 87/87, frame target 48 vs ours 56. NO source edit was made this pass — the two newest applicable laws were screened and both failed their preconditions by measurement, so no probe was spent and the 3-attempt budget was not touched. RESIDUAL DECOMPOSITION, sharper than the prior parks recorded: regnorm reports 106 paired, 0 renaming, 0 unpaired, 9 STRUCTURAL — but only FIVE of those nine are real. The five are one single mechanism, the uniform +8 frame plumbing (stwu -48/-56, stmw r27,28/36, lmw r27,28/36, lwz r0,52/60, addi r1,48/56). The other FOUR are jumptable_8012783C and jumptable_80127808 against @83/@84, i.e. reloc-ANNOTATION rows of the local-symbol name normalization that AGENTS.md already exempts from the EXACT bar and that no source change can or should close. FREE EVIDENCE THE PRIOR PARKS DID NOT STATE, from the aligned fnasm --diff view: every instruction in the body is byte-identical, and stmw r27 saves five registers = 20 bytes ending exactly at the frame top on BOTH sides, so this function has NO memory-resident local at all (the slots slotdiff reports at 48/52 target and 56/60 ours are the caller's linkage and LR words above the stwu, not locals). The frame is therefore exactly 8 linkage + dead region + 20 saves, giving a dead region of 20 in the target and 28 in ours — which independently reproduces the prior parks' '20 vs 28' figure from the instruction stream alone.
